biography.plain_text: The Government of Egypt is the executive and administrative authority of the Arab Republic of Egypt. Working through the Cabinet and ministries, it develops public policy, implements legislation and directs state administration. The name represents the continuing government as a public institution rather than the president, prime minister, a particular ministry or any individual officeholder.

long_biography.plain_text:
Egypt’s Cabinet forms the central framework for national executive administration. Led by the prime minister, ministers direct portfolios covering the state’s major policy and service responsibilities, coordinate government programmes and oversee the work of their ministries.

The government operates as a continuing institution even when presidents, prime ministers or cabinet members change. Its administrative identity encompasses the collective machinery responsible for implementing legislation and managing national policy across the Arab Republic of Egypt. The name therefore belongs to the institutional government and not to any individual officeholder, ministry, department or public official.
